# Requirements Document: A flight the airline cancels

## Introduction

When the airline cancels a flight and does not move the customer to another
one, the services on that flight become cancelled with delivery status
UNABLE TO DELIVER.  The worked example changes no order item's status and
offers no refund.  No source says whether the customer is owed money back, or
how much of an item's price belongs to one of its flights, since the price is
set per order item.  The model takes the refund as a parameter, a reading of
the sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/FlightCancel.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/FlightCancel.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-704

**User Story:** As a customer whose flight the airline cancelled, I want the cancelled services marked and their value returned, so that I do not pay for a flight that will not operate.

**Rule:** WHEN the airline cancels a flight and does not re-accommodate the customer THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel every live service on that flight with delivery status UNABLE TO DELIVER. (Lean: `cancelFlight`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the airline cancels a flight and does not re-accommodate the customer THE SYSTEM SHALL mark CANCELLED with delivery status UNABLE TO DELIVER every live service on that flight, in every order item, that the delivery status table lets become UNABLE TO DELIVER.
   - ONE-704.1, proven: proven theorem `cancel_flight_marks`; example `cancelBothFlights`; example `cancelFlightWhileRequested`; example `cancelInboundFlight`
2. WHEN the airline cancels a flight THE SYSTEM SHALL leave every service on other flights unchanged.
   - ONE-704.2, proven: proven theorem `cancel_flight_keeps_others`; example `cancelInboundFlight`
3. WHEN the airline cancels a flight THE SYSTEM SHALL keep every order item with its reference and price.
   - ONE-704.3, proven: proven theorem `cancel_flight_keeps_items`; example `cancelInboundFlight`
4. IF the airline cancels a flight of a paid order item and does not re-accommodate the customer THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refund the customer part of the item's price.
   - ONE-704.4, open: open theorem `cancel_flight_refunds`; counterexample `cancelBothFlights`; counterexample `cancelInboundFlight`
5. WHEN the airline cancels a flight THE SYSTEM SHALL mark CANCELLED every order item that holds a CANCELLED service.
   - ONE-704.5, open: open theorem `cancel_flight_cancelled_items`; counterexample `cancelBothFlights`; counterexample `cancelInboundFlight`
6. WHEN the airline cancels a flight and does not re-accommodate the customer THE SYSTEM SHALL leave no live service on that flight.
   - ONE-704.6, open: open theorem `cancel_flight_leaves_no_live`; counterexample `cancelFlightWhileRequested`

#### Open question on ONE-704.4

> When the airline cancels a flight of a paid order item and does not
> re-accommodate the customer, the customer gets part of the item's price back.
>
> Open question for the business.  The flight cancellation worked example
> offers no follow-up action and no refund, and no source says whether a flight
> the airline cannot deliver entitles the customer to money back.  Because the
> price is set per order item, no source says how much of it belongs to one
> flight either.  Under the reading the worked example shows, a paid return trip
> at 1,000.00 EUR whose inbound flight is cancelled gets nothing back.  The
> example `cancelInboundFlight` shows it.  Is a refund owed when the
> airline cancels a flight without re-accommodation, and how much of an item's
> price belongs to that flight?

#### Open question on ONE-704.5

> After the airline cancels a flight, every order item that holds a
> CANCELLED service is itself CANCELLED, provided this held before.
>
> Open question for the business.  The Order concept ties a CANCELLED service
> to a cancelled order item, and the cancellation page treats cancelling some
> services of an item as a change.  The flight cancellation worked example
> cancels one flight's services and leaves the item as it was.  A return trip
> whose inbound flight is cancelled keeps an active outbound flight, so the item
> stays ACTIVE with CANCELLED services in it, under every reading.  The example
> `cancelInboundFlight` shows it.  Should the airline replace the item, as
> a change does, or may an active item hold cancelled services?

#### Open question on ONE-704.6

> When the airline cancels a flight and does not re-accommodate the
> customer, no live service is left on that flight.
>
> Open question for the business.  The flight's services are ended through the
> delivery status table, and the table has no move to UNABLE TO DELIVER from
> REQUESTED, IN PROGRESS or SUSPENDED, under any reading.  A service the airline
> has not yet confirmed therefore stays live on a flight that will not operate.
> The example `cancelFlightWhileRequested` shows it.  What delivery status
> does a requested, in-progress or suspended service take when its flight is
> cancelled?
